translations.text: Rebuke us in his place [?]. This too is the way in which someone is [?].

[?] All the more so is the person among you who will say, “God will forgive those who do, or will do, those abominable deeds in his congregations after they have acquired all this knowledge and heard all these words.”

For it is easier, O people who have wanted this because of the impurity of their souls, for the one telling you these things to be of one mind with tax collectors, sexually immoral people, and all evildoers, if they turn away
from their unjust or defiling deeds, than to be of one mind with you, because you are turning away from purity and truthful deeds toward defilement and deceitful deeds.
Was it not under extreme distress, because of those who had also committed pernicious deeds before today, that I spoke these words on a day of affliction,
when we were gathered together: “Am I to gather together or offer up the offering with impure people who commit pernicious deeds?
Or how difficult is it for someone who speaks the truth to assemble with tax collectors, prostitutes, and all the wicked, or to offer the offering with them?

[?] Not because they have turned away from their evil deeds—or rather, because they have not turned away from them—but because no judgment falls upon him if he assembles or offers the offering with them. For they have not been entrusted to him, so that he should be questioned about them.

How, in turn, will it not be difficult for someone to whom people have been entrusted to assemble with impure people who commit corrupt deeds among them, or to offer offerings with them, when their blood and their judgment fall upon him?
“Rather, their condemnation and their blood are upon the congregation itself.” For not only is the soul of the one in charge of them not in agreement with those who commit that evil
among you, but it is also laid down for him, through the rule and the decision established by God—as it has been from the beginning until now—that he must not eat bread
or drink water or gather with the whole congregation to pray or present the offering until he has brought their judgment upon their heads, their blood upon their own midst.
because someone might again dare to commit such abominable deeds in the Lord’s congregations, among our holy brothers who guard themselves against every defilement and every deceitful deed.
It will not happen again this time, or in the remaining days, as it has often happened within you, O congregation, with disturbances, retreats, and harsh deeds—

the days that the one speaking with you will spend alive. Rather, those who are shown to him to have committed pernicious deeds within you, he will exclude from you, without disturbance and without shouting.

And if there are others within you who deceitfully commit abominable deeds without being known to us, whether male or female, great or small, they are left in the hands of God’s wrath, for him to punish them in his anger.

For anyone whom you do not know to be committing pernicious deeds within you—the curses themselves that are written in the Scriptures, together with the curses in the books written for us, know them and know how to deal with them, with all their torments.

As for the belts and bandages that this man took off and laid down because they had not been useful to him, or had become useless, or had no use left in them, you will see some of them in one condition at one time, and another portion

in another condition, another portion like this, and another portion like that, so that you may understand, brothers, that this man did not wrap himself in so much cloth or so many bandages for any other reason than the matter that he himself knows.

If the bandages or belts that have worn out, so that they are no longer useful to me or suitable for wrapping myself in during the illness in my body—or the body—are numerous in the eyes of the one who knows their number, the belts or bandages that you will see

lying discarded, with no use left in them, are more numerous than those that have become useless. Yet they will seem few to you, because their ruined appearance makes it impossible to tell which is which, or this one from that one, so that someone could count them or state their number.

And they will be in the place [?]—I myself do not know who it is—who hid them there beneath the earth, in the place where the abyss, or the abysses, opened, filled with every useless thing, until the time when you see them with your own eyes.

For everything that this man who is speaking to you, congregation, did before today, he did because he wanted to remove the shame from those who do these corrupt deeds among us, turning it back upon himself, because he loves his neighbor as himself.
But now he himself is removing it from himself and turning it back upon everyone who does or will do abominable things deceitfully or secretly, whether male or female.
And their shame is upon them, for it rests upon them and is plainly visible upon them, and they are exposed as having it upon them.
And honoring them again in the presence of this man who is now distressed [?], in the same way—especially a blow with a staff in his hand—from today onward is a shame to him himself.

This statement is not about my esteemed brothers or beloved children, because of their purity and their love for God. Rather, it concerns those whom this holy place does not benefit and who gain no benefit in it, because they are destroying their hope, as we said earlier.
Were not these places, or every congregation gathered in them because of God's name, called holy places?
Then how cursed will those be who defile them with shameful deeds!
Or was this saying not enough for those miserable wretches, when it cut them off from life once and for all: “The children who have become defiled are not his”?
Or is there still greater wrath than this that God will bring upon whoever destroys his temple: “Whoever destroys God's temple, God will destroy him”?

What is easy [?] down to [?] those who fear God in these congregations? With what will he be able to honor them, or with what will he be able to bless them, beyond what the saints said: “Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways.”
You will eat the fruits of your labors.
But the one who is continually grieved over those who commit abominable deeds in these congregations will condemn them with a [?]
even more than what the saints said in anger: “The one who does not fear God will remain in desert places forever, with no one coming to look for him.”
A man whom those living within you, O congregation, have often heard swearing, “I would rather die, or have God call me to account, than hear that someone

has committed pernicious deeds within you”—is it not clear that he is free of that condemnation and of the blood of those who afflict him because they were not ashamed to commit those abominable, ungodly deeds within you?
Oh, what will this place do?
Where will this place go?
Before today, the person or people who knew the measure, or who had measured the evil deeds they had committed within you, [?] will say [?].

They ended by saying that these deeds had reached parts of those who committed them—or rather, had completely overwhelmed them like a great flood, and they had sunk into it like animals. God found us in it in his mercy.
But now, in this present time, those who measure it or take its measurements will say, or are saying, “It reaches the knees [?].”
Yet it has not reached [?], and those who fell into it, or onto it, sank up to their thighs.
Indeed, it is not like that within you now either.
May it never happen!
Nor was there much of it.

But those who fell into it wallowed in it like pigs, not merely until it reached their thighs, or until they sank into it up to their thighs, but until they appeared filthy and smeared with it, from their toenails to the hair on their heads.

If that mud had been deeper at this present time, or if it still reached the thighs according to its former depth, those who saw the people in it would have said, “Certainly they could not get up or come out of it, because it is deep.”
And whoever says that it has not diminished very, very greatly is like someone who sheds blood, because he has insulted the grace that the Lord Jesus Christ has shown us.
But in the final period, in turn, they would not say that the mud reached the ankles, or the knees, or the thighs, but the necks of those who do corrupt deeds in it, whether male or female.

And again, this other expression, “measure” or “take measurements,” is not only written at the beginning of the first sheet set down from the outset, measuring or taking measurements of what exists or what has happened within you or to you, O synagogue; it is also there again:

“They have taken account of what you did not know or understand, and those who came to learn about or see the things that have happened to you have taken account of what shook you, in the enclosed and hidden places that are full of darkness, or are dark within you.”

But if someone asks, “What are these measurements or this taking of measurements? Who are those who took measurements? Or what did they measure?” let him tell us, or let him tell me, how the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was measured with a reed,
and who measured it, and why they measured it or marked out its boundaries. Was it, then, in sorrow?
Or, if not, why such great reassurance? And again, on what grounds did the prophet Zechariah say, “I will take two staffs for myself, calling one Beauty and calling the second Cord”? And

was it, then, in mercy and compassion—or rather in anger and wrath—that he said afterward, “I will take my beautiful staff and throw it away, to break the covenant that I established with all the peoples.
And they will be destroyed in those days, and the Canaanites will recognize [?] the sheep that trust in me, because it is the word of the Lord.”
Then again: “I threw away the second staff, Cord, to break the covenant between Judah and Jerusalem.”
And again, whether in consolation or rather in rebuke, Micah the prophet also said: “They measured out my people's portion with a measuring line for a field.”

And whether those who measured that portion were from God, like the one who measured the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, and as with the designation of the two staffs, Beauty and Cord, which we mentioned earlier, or whether they were from...
